memos.headline: JPM Near Highs With Low Volatility Leads the Tape; MSFT Overbought After Parabolic Move; CAT Breaking Down
memos.body: I see a clear split in this universe today. JPM is the cleanest chart: just 0.5% off its 52-week high, RSI 63 (healthy, not stretched), ATR only 1.89%, and relative strength vs SPY of +12.5% over 12 weeks — textbook leadership with low volatility. MSFT has been spectacular (+29.8% in 4 weeks, RSI 78.1, +22.8% above its 50-day mean) but that extension is unsustainable short-term and I'd wait for a pullback toward the 50-day before adding. On the weak side, CAT is in a confirmed downtrend: -20.9% drawdown from highs, -8.1% below its 50-day, RSI 42.9, and relative strength vs SPY of -14% over 4 weeks — I'd avoid until it reclaims its 50-day mean near ~916. PG and GOOGL are both languishing below their 50-day means with negative relative strength, offering no reason to own them here.

views.note: Sitting 0.5% from 52w high with RSI 63, low ATR 1.89%, and strong 12w relative strength of +12.5% vs SPY; would reassess on a close below 340.
Massive +29.8% 4w rally has RSI at 78.1 and price 22.8% above 50d mean — too extended to chase; would turn long on a pullback toward ~410 (50d area).
Only 3.4% off highs with positive 4w relative strength of +9.5% vs SPY and RSI 64 — constructive trend; invalidated below 250.
Strong 11.6% weekly bounce, just 5% off highs with RSI 64, though 12w relative strength vs SPY is -3.3% so conviction is moderate; would cut below 205.

12w relative strength vs SPY is -13.3%, 12% off highs, and sitting right at its 50d mean with no momentum — no edge here until it clears 370.
Trading below both 50d and 200d means, 12.8% off highs, negative 26w return of -3.9% — persistent underperformance with no sign of a turn.
Huge 26w gain of +41.9% but near-term momentum has faded with RSI 44 and -6.6% 4w relative strength; watching for support near 395 to hold.
Flat near 50d mean with RSI 47.6 and negative 4w relative strength of -3.1% vs SPY — no clear directional signal; need a break above 340 or below 295 to act.
Decent 4w relative strength of +7.8% but 12w relative strength is -3.2% and still 10.7% off highs — mixed signals, watching for a close above 160 to turn constructive.

memos.headline: Mega-cap tech delivers extraordinary earnings growth; XOM, PG, and UNH show cash-flow compression risk
memos.body: I am struck by the sheer breadth of earnings acceleration across the large-cap tech complex this quarter. GOOGL posted a 93.7% net margin on $119.8B of revenue with net income up nearly 298% YoY—likely driven by a large one-time gain, but even adjusting for that the top-line +24.2% growth is impressive. NVDA continues to dominate with 85.2% YoY revenue growth and a 71.5% net margin on $81.6B of revenue, while AMZN's net income surged 245% YoY to $62.65B on a 31.2% margin, a dramatic profitability inflection. On the other side, I see clear earnings deterioration at XOM (net income down 45.8% YoY on a razor-thin 4.9% margin), PG (net income down 15.8% on only 1.5% revenue growth), and UNH (flat net income with 2.0% revenue growth and heavy $77.9B debt load). A reversal in margin trends at AMZN or NVDA—specifically if AMZN's net margin falls back below 15% or NVDA's revenue growth decelerates below 30%—would change my view on those names.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY to $81.6B with 71.5% net margin and only $8.5B debt—unmatched earnings power and balance sheet strength.
Net income exploded +245% YoY to $62.65B with margin expanding to 31.2%, though $133B debt warrants monitoring.
Full-year Q4 revenue of $90B (+17.7% YoY) with 39.7% net margin and net income +31.3% shows durable, high-quality earnings growth.
Revenue +24.2% YoY is strong but the 93.7% net margin likely includes a large non-recurring item, so I need to see the breakdown before raising conviction.
Revenue +24% YoY to $20.5B with net income +65% and a healthy 17.5% margin signals a strong industrial cycle, though $36B debt is elevated.
Revenue +27.7% and net income +41.2% are impressive for a bank, but $460B total debt and cyclical sensitivity keep me at neutral.
Revenue +16.4% and net income +27.1% are solid, but $82.3B debt and a 27.2% margin leave less upside versus peers like MSFT and NVDA.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a 4.9% margin with only 2.4% revenue growth—clear earnings compression.
Net income fell 15.8% YoY on anemic 1.5% revenue growth with margin contracting to 14.4%, signaling no pricing power or volume growth.
Flat net income (-0.2% YoY) on only 2.0% revenue growth with $77.9B debt suggests stagnating earnings power and leverage risk.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 3.75% but Sticky 3.5% CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue Against Duration and Favor Defensives
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode—the upper bound has sat at 3.75% for three months despite 75 bps of cuts over the prior year, and the effective rate is essentially flat at 3.63%. The problem is inflation: CPI is running 3.5% y/y as of June, well above target, which explains why the 10-year yield has climbed 42 bps over the past year to 4.65% and the 2s10s curve has actually flattened 9 bps to +44 bps. The labor market is not forcing the Fed's hand either way—unemployment at 4.2% ticked down 10 bps over three months, signaling no imminent recession but no overheating. My regime call is 'pause with hawkish tilt': further cuts are off the table until CPI convincingly breaks below 3%, and a re-hike cannot be ruled out. A July CPI print above 0.3% m/m or unemployment breaking below 4.0% would push me toward an outright hawkish regime shift.

views.note: Duration-sensitive mega-cap growth faces headwinds from the 4.65% 10y yield, but stable labor market supports consumer demand; net neutral.
Similar duration exposure as AAPL; rising real rates cap multiples, but recurring revenue provides some insulation.
Highest-duration name in the universe is most vulnerable if the 10y continues to grind higher with sticky inflation at 3.5% y/y.
Positive 2s10s slope of 44 bps supports NIM, Fed pause keeps short rates elevated, and 4.2% unemployment limits credit losses.
Sticky inflation historically supports real assets, but no direct energy data in hand; macro backdrop is mildly supportive, not compelling.
Defensive staples with pricing power benefit from a pause regime and 3.5% CPI environment where consumers still spend but growth decelerates.
Cyclical bellwether faces mixed signals—labor market is fine but rising long rates and a flattening curve suggest late-cycle caution.
Consumer-facing strength from low unemployment offsets duration headwind from elevated 10y yields; balanced risk.
Ad revenue tied to nominal GDP which sticky inflation supports, but higher discount rates limit multiple expansion.
Defensive healthcare with pricing leverage in an inflationary pause regime; less rate-sensitive than growth tech.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Split: MSFT and AMZN Surge While AAPL and GOOGL Sell Off Hard
memos.body: I am reading a stark divergence in market-revealed sentiment across mega-cap tech following the Q2/Q3 earnings wave. MSFT (+15.5%) and AMZN (+15.3%) saw massive positive price reactions to their earnings 8-Ks filed 7/29 and 7/30 respectively, signaling genuine narrative upgrades that likely still have momentum given the magnitude of the moves. Conversely, AAPL (-7.4%) and GOOGL (-7.1%) suffered sharp post-earnings selloffs, suggesting disappointed expectations and a negative tone shift that may linger. CAT's +5.6% reaction to its 8/4 earnings print is a quieter positive signal in industrials, while JPM (+2.5% on 7/14) and UNH (+1.2% on 7/16) showed muted but constructive reactions that are likely already fully priced a few weeks later. I have highest conviction on the MSFT/AMZN long side and the AAPL avoid side, with less conviction on names where the earnings reaction was small or stale.

views.note: A +15.5% earnings-day move is a rare magnitude signal indicating a genuine positive narrative shift that likely has follow-through.
The +15.3% post-earnings reaction on 7/30-7/31 signals a strong positive sentiment inflection with likely residual momentum.
A -7.4% earnings selloff just one week ago suggests negative sentiment is fresh and likely not yet fully absorbed.
The -7.1% post-earnings drop on 7/22-7/23 reflects a meaningful negative tone shift, though two weeks of digestion reduces conviction somewhat.
A solid +5.6% earnings reaction on 8/4 is a constructive signal, though lower magnitude and industrial-sector context temper conviction.
The +2.5% earnings reaction on 7/14 was modest and is now three weeks stale, likely fully priced.
A mild -1.9% earnings reaction suggests no strong sentiment catalyst in either direction.
No earnings reaction data available yet; recent 8-Ks are governance/housekeeping items with no clear sentiment signal.
The +1.2% earnings reaction on 7/16 was tepid and is now three weeks old, offering no actionable sentiment edge.
The 7/1 8-K covers an acquisition/disposition event, not earnings; no clear directional sentiment read available.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Rising but Credit Calm: Oil Spike and Export-Control Overhang Shape Positioning
memos.body: I see a divergence worth flagging: the Economic Policy Uncertainty index has climbed 7.5% over the past month to 262, yet VIX has continued to fall (15.15, down ~13% over three months) and HY spreads are essentially flat at 2.71%. This tells me markets are pricing geopolitical noise as manageable, but the policy uncertainty uptick—likely tied to ongoing trade and technology-control debates—could still bite names with heavy China or energy exposure. WTI's 13.3% one-month surge to $78.88 despite a 20% three-month decline suggests a supply disruption or sanctions-related tightening rather than demand strength, which benefits XOM near-term but signals fragility. I have moderate conviction that NVDA remains the most exposed to any escalation in export controls, while PG's defensive profile and limited geopolitical surface area make it a relative safe harbor. A formal broadening of semiconductor export restrictions or new energy sanctions would be the catalysts that change my views materially.

views.note: Rising policy uncertainty and the structural overhang of potential tighter AI-chip export controls to China keep me sidelined despite strong demand trends.
WTI's sharp 13.3% one-month rally to ~$79 supports near-term earnings, though the 20% three-month decline signals demand or sanctions-related volatility that limits conviction.
Minimal geopolitical exposure and defensive demand profile make PG attractive when policy uncertainty is elevated at 262; recent Reg FD filings suggest steady operational messaging.
CAT's Reg FD disclosure days before this note and its sensitivity to trade-policy shifts and infrastructure spending keep me neutral until clarity improves.
A steepening yield curve (+9 bps in one month to 0.44%) and tight credit spreads favor large-bank earnings, and multiple recent 8-Ks suggest active capital-markets activity.
No fresh 8-K filings and persistent China supply-chain concentration risk amid elevated policy uncertainty warrant a wait-and-see stance.
